blocks.text: Dohra:

(Dear readers) listen to the episode about the city of Kasur1 , The way the Dal Khalsa Singhs occupied Kasur for the first time. And the way the Pathan custodians of Kasur had been defeated, Who had turned defiant even against the Lahore rulers. (1)
lines: (Dear readers) listen to the episode about the city of Kasur1 ,
The way the Dal Khalsa Singhs occupied Kasur for the first time.
And the way the Pathan custodians of Kasur had been defeated,
Who had turned defiant even against the Lahore rulers.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

It was in the year eignteen hundred and seventeen2 (B.S.), That the Dal Khalsa forces put up a camp near the Amritsar shrine. After having a dip in the holy pool on the day of Baisakhi, Half the Khalsa forces moved to places across the river Beas. (2)
lines: It was in the year eignteen hundred and seventeen2 (B.S.),
That the Dal Khalsa forces put up a camp near the Amritsar shrine.
After having a dip in the holy pool on the day of Baisakhi,
Half the Khalsa forces moved to places across the river Beas.

blocks.text: Five of the Khalsa contingents/Misls stayed up at Amritsar, Which included Misls of Ramgharias, Ghanaiyyas Shukarchakkias3 and Nakais, Hari Singh Bhangi, chief of the Bhangi Misl too stayed there, Who put up his camp in his own fort at Amritsar. (3)
lines: Five of the Khalsa contingents/Misls stayed up at Amritsar,
Which included Misls of Ramgharias,
Ghanaiyyas Shukarchakkias3 and Nakais,
Hari Singh Bhangi, chief of the Bhangi Misl too stayed there,
Who put up his camp in his own fort at Amritsar.

blocks.text: Daily in the afternoon would he pay obeisance at Akal Takht, Daily would he return to his fort after the evening prayer.
Everyday, without fail, would he pay his obeisance, Be it raining or be it a day of winds blowing. (4)
lines: Everyday, without fail, would he pay his obeisance,
Be it raining or be it a day of winds blowing.

blocks.text: So would all the Khalsa Panth Singhs pay their obeisance, So would they return to their camps after the evening congregation. Without nursing any ill-will and malice towards anyone, Would the Khalsa confabulate in the congregation. (5)
lines: So would all the Khalsa Panth Singhs pay their obeisance,
So would they return to their camps after the evening congregation.
Without nursing any ill-will and malice towards anyone,
Would the Khalsa confabulate in the congregation.

blocks.text: Dohra:
During one of those days at the sacred shrine, Was Hari Singh Bhangi sitting in the congregation. There arrived a Brahmin from the city of Kasur, Who raised a hue and cry in the congregation. (6)
lines: During one of those days at the sacred shrine,
Was Hari Singh Bhangi sitting in the congregation.
There arrived a Brahmin from the city of Kasur,
Who raised a hue and cry in the congregation.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In a voice raised high did this Brahmin plead, That his spouse had been abducted by Kasur Pathans. The Khalsa having been created for the protection of the Hindus, It was their moral duty as Kshtriyas of Guru Nanak's dynasty. (7)
lines: In a voice raised high did this Brahmin plead,
That his spouse had been abducted by Kasur Pathans.
The Khalsa having been created for the protection of the Hindus,
It was their moral duty as Kshtriyas of Guru Nanak's dynasty.

blocks.text: An act of immense tyranny had the Kasur Muslims committed, Surely had they paved a way for their own annihilation. That protection of the Khalsa Panth had he sought, In such words did he raise a hue and cry. (8)
lines: An act of immense tyranny had the Kasur Muslims committed,
Surely had they paved a way for their own annihilation.
That protection of the Khalsa Panth had he sought,
In such words did he raise a hue and cry.

blocks.text: Leaving the Khalsa Panth's protection where else should he go, Which other court should he knock at for justice? Laying down his turban at the Khalsa Panth's feet, He threatened to commit suicide if was refused protection. (9)
lines: Leaving the Khalsa Panth's protection where else should he go,
Which other court should he knock at for justice?
Laying down his turban at the Khalsa Panth's feet,
He threatened to commit suicide if was refused protection.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Addressing the desperately pleading Brahmin, Hari Singh Bhangi asked him to present himself the next day. He must put forth his petition in the Khalsa congregation, After the daily recitation of the evening prayer was concluded. (10)
lines: Addressing the desperately pleading Brahmin,
Hari Singh Bhangi asked him to present himself the next day.
He must put forth his petition in the Khalsa congregation,
After the daily recitation of the evening prayer was concluded.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The next day did he present himself in the Khalsa congregation, After having a dip in sacred pool did he present himself. After paying obeisance did he sit among the Singhs, With rapt attention did he listen to the Gurbani hymns. (11)
lines: The next day did he present himself in the Khalsa congregation,
After having a dip in sacred pool did he present himself.
After paying obeisance did he sit among the Singhs,
With rapt attention did he listen to the Gurbani hymns.

blocks.text: As soon as the evening prayer concluded after the recitation, The Brahmin repeated his plea amidst tears and cries. Must the Khalsa make efforts to redress his grievance, Must the Khalsa destroy Kasur to set things right. (12)
lines: As soon as the evening prayer concluded after the recitation,
The Brahmin repeated his plea amidst tears and cries.
Must the Khalsa make efforts to redress his grievance,
Must the Khalsa destroy Kasur to set things right.

blocks.text: Else would he commit suicide before the congregation, Surely would that bring ignominy to the Khalsa Panth. Thereupon, Hari Singh Bhangi put a poser to the congregation, Must the congregation respond in whatever way they deemed proper. (13)
lines: Else would he commit suicide before the congregation,
Surely would that bring ignominy to the Khalsa Panth.
Thereupon,
Hari Singh Bhangi put a poser to the congregation,
Must the congregation respond in whatever way they deemed proper.

blocks.text: Thereupon the whole congregation responded in one voice, That Hari Singh Bhangi himself was the most sensible among them. But must the Singhs reckon their own and the Pathan's strength, Even as the Brahmin kept repeating his appeal. (14)
lines: Thereupon the whole congregation responded in one voice,
That Hari Singh Bhangi himself was the most sensible among them.
But must the Singhs reckon their own and the Pathan's strength,
Even as the Brahmin kept repeating his appeal.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon, Hari Singh consulted a few war veterans, After calling a meeting of those veterans next day. He asked them to give him their own assessment, After evaluating the Kasur Pathans' strength verses their own. (15)
lines: Thereupon,
Hari Singh consulted a few war veterans,
After calling a meeting of those veterans next day.
He asked them to give him their own assessment,
After evaluating the Kasur Pathans' strength verses their own.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, the elderly Singhs gave their opinion after evaluation, That the Singhs were in minority as compared to the Pathans. The Singhs' strength under his command was just five thousand, As the rest had gone on a visit to their own homes. (16)
lines: Thereafter, the elderly Singhs gave their opinion after evaluation,
That the Singhs were in minority as compared to the Pathans.
The Singhs' strength under his command was just five thousand,
As the rest had gone on a visit to their own homes.

blocks.text: As far as the strength of the rest of the four Sikh Misls, Their combined strength did not exceed eight thousand. The Muslims forces in Kasur province stood at twelve lakhs, Which were stationed at twelve different forts. (17)
lines: As far as the strength of the rest of the four Sikh Misls,
Their combined strength did not exceed eight thousand.
The Muslims forces in Kasur province stood at twelve lakhs,
Which were stationed at twelve different forts.

blocks.text: Many forts and encircling deep-water channels had they made, Many formations of canons and small guns have they deployed. Defiant indeed these Kasur Pathans had turned against Lahore, With two of the ministers of theirs possessing wealth in crores. (18)
lines: Many forts and encircling deep-water channels had they made,
Many formations of canons and small guns have they deployed.
Defiant indeed these Kasur Pathans had turned against Lahore,
With two of the ministers of theirs possessing wealth in crores.

blocks.text: Fleeing Lahore had these ministers entered Kasur when Abdali invaded, Well entranched did they stay in Kasur during the Maratha invasion, As these Pathans had harassed even the (mighty) Ahmad Shah Abdali, How could the Singhs ever think of overpowering these Pathans. (19)
lines: Fleeing Lahore had these ministers entered Kasur when Abdali invaded,
Well entranched did they stay in Kasur during the Maratha invasion,
As these Pathans had harassed even the (mighty) Ahmad Shah Abdali,
How could the Singhs ever think of overpowering these Pathans.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon, did Hari Singh declare in a bold voice, "This encounter shall now definitely take place." Certainly would Hari Singh make his own sacrifice, If, perchance, Kasur remained unconquered by the Khalsa. (20)
lines: Thereupon, did Hari Singh declare in a bold voice,
"This encounter shall now definitely take place." Certainly would Hari Singh make his own sacrifice,
If, perchance,
Kasur remained unconquered by the Khalsa.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, did the Khslas congregation declare unanimously, The whole Khalsa Panth would follow his footsteps. They pleaded him to accept one of their suggestions, That he must seek the support of Buddha Dal Singhs. (21)
lines: Thereupon, did the Khslas congregation declare unanimously,
The whole Khalsa Panth would follow his footsteps.
They pleaded him to accept one of their suggestions,
That he must seek the support of Buddha Dal Singhs.

blocks.text: Thereupon, Hari Singh Bhangi remarked once again, How long would they keep waiting for the arrival of Buddha Dal? Thereupon did S. Charat Singh said brandishing his sword, Must the Khalsa launch an attack on Kasur without delay. (22)
lines: Thereupon,
Hari Singh Bhangi remarked once again,
How long would they keep waiting for the arrival of Buddha Dal?
Thereupon did S.
Charat Singh said brandishing his sword,
Must the Khalsa launch an attack on Kasur without delay.

blocks.text: Must there be the hand of Divine providence behind this, That a Brahmin had been chosen to deliver this message. Must the Khalsa seek guidance from Guru's word at random4 , Surely would the Guru's word reveal this mission's success or failure. (23)
lines: Must there be the hand of Divine providence behind this,
That a Brahmin had been chosen to deliver this message.
Must the Khalsa seek guidance from Guru's word at random4 ,
Surely would the Guru's word reveal this mission's success or failure.

blocks.text: Really did this suggestion appeal to all the Ghaniyya Misl Singhs, Equally did it appeal to the Singhs of the Ramgharia Misl. Fully acceptable was it to the Singhs of Nakai Misl as well, Really indeed would it have been the will of the Divine Lord. (24)
lines: Really did this suggestion appeal to all the Ghaniyya Misl Singhs,
Equally did it appeal to the Singhs of the Ramgharia Misl.
Fully acceptable was it to the Singhs of Nakai Misl as well,
Really indeed would it have been the will of the Divine Lord.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As everyone in the Khalsa congregation approved of the suggestion, The whole congregation moved to listen to the Guru's word at random. Surely would the Guru indicate what was to be happened, Be it a victory or defeat for the Khalsa Panth forces. (25)
lines: As everyone in the Khalsa congregation approved of the suggestion,
The whole congregation moved to listen to the Guru's word at random.
Surely would the Guru indicate what was to be happened,
Be it a victory or defeat for the Khalsa Panth forces.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, the whole Khalsa congregation went to Darbar Sahib, With folded hands and a single prayer they stood before the Guru. They being the Guru's followers and the Guru being their Divine Lord, They begged the Guru to indicate what was His Divine Will. (26)
lines: Thereupon, the whole Khalsa congregation went to Darbar Sahib,
With folded hands and a single prayer they stood before the Guru.
They being the Guru's followers and the Guru being their Divine Lord,
They begged the Guru to indicate what was His Divine Will.

blocks.text: Must the Guru indicate the destruction of the city of Kasur, Provided His Divine Will approved of His followers' cause. Thus with folded hands the whole gathering stood, With some still prostrating after paying their obeisance. (27)
lines: Must the Guru indicate the destruction of the city of Kasur,
Provided His Divine Will approved of His followers' cause.
Thus with folded hands the whole gathering stood,
With some still prostrating after paying their obeisance.

blocks.text: Guru Granth Sahib being the true embodiment of the Sikh Gurus, Must it provide a true direction to the Sikh congregation. As the head priest looked at the text after turning over a page, It was the turn of hymn in the "Raga Basant" which read as follow: (28)
lines: Guru Granth Sahib being the true embodiment of the Sikh Gurus,
Must it provide a true direction to the Sikh congregation.
As the head priest looked at the text after turning over a page,
It was the turn of hymn in the "Raga Basant" which read as follow:

blocks.text: Pauri:

With the support and protection from the true Lord, Have I put the five most powerful demons6 under leash. With His Divine presence lodged within my mind, Has he made me meditate upon His lotus feet (Divine). Wth all the affictions and frustrations wiped out, Have I become hale and hearty forever indeed. With meditating upon His Name day and night, Have I got liberated from death again and again, With the true instruction from the true Lord,
Has Nanak received comfort and happiness.
Dohra:

So much delighted the Khalsa felt after listening to Guru's word, As if they had already taken over the city of Kasur. Khalsa slogans of victory did they shout out of joy, As if they were already beating war drums of victory. (29)
lines: So much delighted the Khalsa felt after listening to Guru's word,
As if they had already taken over the city of Kasur.
Khalsa slogans of victory did they shout out of joy,
As if they were already beating war drums of victory.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hari Singh Bhangi, somehow, spending the night at Amritsar, Khalsa march did he order early in the morning. He, having listened to the Guru's word from the Guru, No astrologer did he consult for any auspicious moment. (30)
lines: Hari Singh Bhangi, somehow, spending the night at Amritsar,
Khalsa march did he order early in the morning.
He, having listened to the Guru's word from the Guru,
No astrologer did he consult for any auspicious moment.

blocks.text: With Khalsa putting up the first camp at a place Pipli, Excellently prepared five thousand Sikh warriors were they indeed. With the forces from the four other Misls joining them here, Nearly ten thousand excellent horses did they possess. (31)
lines: With Khalsa putting up the first camp at a place Pipli,
Excellently prepared five thousand Sikh warriors were they indeed.
With the forces from the four other Misls joining them here,
Nearly ten thousand excellent horses did they possess.

blocks.text: Hari Singh dispatched dispatches to the Singhs all around, That the Khalsa was lauching a crusade for the protection of Brahmins. Whosoever was keen to uphold the Khalsa Panth's dignity, Must he join this Khalsa crusade to do or die for the cause. (32)
lines: Hari Singh dispatched dispatches to the Singhs all around,
That the Khalsa was lauching a crusade for the protection of Brahmins.
Whosoever was keen to uphold the Khalsa Panth's dignity,
Must he join this Khalsa crusade to do or die for the cause.

blocks.text: Ordering the forces' march after dispatching such epistles, They put up a second camp at Guru-ki-Wadali7 . Nearly five thousand more Singhs joined the Khalsa force here, Really great warriors and devout at heart were they indeed. (33)
lines: Ordering the forces' march after dispatching such epistles,
They put up a second camp at Guru-ki-Wadali7 .
Nearly five thousand more Singhs joined the Khalsa force here,
Really great warriors and devout at heart were they indeed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Beginning their march further from Guru-ki-Wadali, They put up the next camp at the town of Raja Taal8 . Nearly four thousand more joined the Khalsa force, Voluntarily did they become a part and parcel of the Khalsa. (34)
lines: Beginning their march further from Guru-ki-Wadali,
They put up the next camp at the town of Raja Taal8 .
Nearly four thousand more joined the Khalsa force,
Voluntarily did they become a part and parcel of the Khalsa.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Merely four thousand and twenty was the Khalsa in number, Full twelve lakhs were the Kasuri Pathans in strength. So huge being the difference between the two combatants, Terribly concerned did the elderly veterans feel at this disparity. (35)
lines: Merely four thousand and twenty was the Khalsa in number,
Full twelve lakhs were the Kasuri Pathans in strength.
So huge being the difference between the two combatants,
Terribly concerned did the elderly veterans feel at this disparity.

blocks.text: Despite such a large statistical difference would Hari Singh not budge, So much did S. Charat Singh do to boost Hari Singh's morale. But the difference in numerical strength of the two armies disheartened the cowards, Who reckoned never could the Khalsa ever conquer Kasur. (36)
lines: Despite such a large statistical difference would Hari Singh not budge,
So much did S.
Charat Singh do to boost Hari Singh's morale.
But the difference in numerical strength of the two armies disheartened the cowards,
Who reckoned never could the Khalsa ever conquer Kasur.

blocks.text: Those brave hearts who looked at the bravery quotient of the two armies, They reckoned surely would the Khalsa overpower the Kasur Pathans.
As the cowards displayed their cowardice at this inequality, The Brave hearts believed never would the Khalsa get vanquished. (37)
lines: As the cowards displayed their cowardice at this inequality,
The Brave hearts believed never would the Khalsa get vanquished.

blocks.text: Someone favoured the Khalsa to launch a frontal attack, As being on the defensive and retreat would embolden the Pathans. Someone else opined never would the Khalsa desert, Surely would they make supreme sacrifice for the noble cause. (38)
lines: Someone favoured the Khalsa to launch a frontal attack,
As being on the defensive and retreat would embolden the Pathans.
Someone else opined never would the Khalsa desert,
Surely would they make supreme sacrifice for the noble cause.

blocks.text: Dohra:

However, the cowards made conjectures to the contrary, That No one would bother to consult the Khalsa Panth. As the Singhs would be severely beaten by the other, Everyone would run away in whatever direction they could. (39)
lines: However, the cowards made conjectures to the contrary,
That No one would bother to consult the Khalsa Panth.
As the Singhs would be severely beaten by the other,
Everyone would run away in whatever direction they could.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As militant Singhs had heard Guru Granth's prophetic revelation, They had complete faith in Guru's will in ensuring their victory. As the Khalsa forces assembled at the next location, A Sikh traveler from Kasur happened to pass by them. (40)
lines: As militant Singhs had heard Guru Granth's prophetic revelation,
They had complete faith in Guru's will in ensuring their victory.
As the Khalsa forces assembled at the next location,
A Sikh traveler from Kasur happened to pass by them.

blocks.text: Inviting this wayfaring Singh to come and sit among them, The Khalsa Panth enquired about the real situation in Kasur. The traveling Sikh being a member of the Khalsa fraternity, Must he relate all the facts about Kasur Pathans thoroughly. (41)
lines: Inviting this wayfaring Singh to come and sit among them,
The Khalsa Panth enquired about the real situation in Kasur.
The traveling Sikh being a member of the Khalsa fraternity,
Must he relate all the facts about Kasur Pathans thoroughly.

blocks.text: What did the grapevine in Kasur say about the Khalsa march, What kind of fortifications had the Pathan's put up to defend themselves? Where were the Pathans likely to have an encounter with the Khalsa, Were all these issues being talked about in Kasur? (42)
lines: What did the grapevine in Kasur say about the Khalsa march,
What kind of fortifications had the Pathan's put up to defend themselves?
Where were the Pathans likely to have an encounter with the Khalsa,
Were all these issues being talked about in Kasur?

blocks.text: Thereupon did the traveller Sikh inform the Khalsa gathering, That there was hardly anyone who knew about their move. All the main entrances to the city of Kasur remained open, Thus would he speak truely to that assembly of fraternal Sikhs. (43)
lines: Thereupon did the traveller Sikh inform the Khalsa gathering,
That there was hardly anyone who knew about their move.
All the main entrances to the city of Kasur remained open,
Thus would he speak truely to that assembly of fraternal Sikhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Carefree did the Pathans sleep during the midday hours, Freely did they rest in the basements of their dwellings. Being so arrogant hardly were they conscious of God's ways, So leisurely did they come out of their cells after sunset. (44)
lines: Carefree did the Pathans sleep during the midday hours,
Freely did they rest in the basements of their dwellings.
Being so arrogant hardly were they conscious of God's ways,
So leisurely did they come out of their cells after sunset.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Those being the Islamic days of fasting for the Muslims, So did they avoid partaking of water and exposing to the sun. Being so arrogant and proud of their military might, Never could they imagine about anybody's intrusion into their territory. (45)
lines: Those being the Islamic days of fasting for the Muslims,
So did they avoid partaking of water and exposing to the sun.
Being so arrogant and proud of their military might,
Never could they imagine about anybody's intrusion into their territory.

blocks.text: Hearing this account, did the Singhs feel in their heart of hearts, Surely was Guru Granth Sahib's prediction being fulfilled. Debilitated would have the Pathans become with long fasting, Truly had they made themselves vulnerable to death. (46)
lines: Hearing this account, did the Singhs feel in their heart of hearts,
Surely was Guru Granth Sahib's prediction being fulfilled.
Debilitated would have the Pathans become with long fasting,
Truly had they made themselves vulnerable to death.

blocks.text: At midday noon should the Khalsa Singhs enter the city of Kasur, Silently should they march on without causing any noise. Without unfurling their continental emblems and beating of battle drums, Scrupulously should they avoid robbing wayfarers to maintain secrecy. (47)
lines: At midday noon should the Khalsa Singhs enter the city of Kasur,
Silently should they march on without causing any noise.
Without unfurling their continental emblems and beating of battle drums,
Scrupulously should they avoid robbing wayfarers to maintain secrecy.

blocks.text: Such a resolution did the Khalsa Panth arrive at, That without slaughtering Pathans would they not ransack. From the front would all the Khalsa contingent chiefs lead, As if a delegation of traders had entered the city for trade. (48)
lines: Such a resolution did the Khalsa Panth arrive at,
That without slaughtering Pathans would they not ransack.
From the front would all the Khalsa contingent chiefs lead,
As if a delegation of traders had entered the city for trade.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As some Singhs stood in formations of one here and two there, A few others went ahead into the markets of Kasur city. As some dismounted from their horses and sat inside the shops, Other started making enquiries about the prices of commodities. (49)
lines: As some Singhs stood in formations of one here and two there,
A few others went ahead into the markets of Kasur city.
As some dismounted from their horses and sat inside the shops,
Other started making enquiries about the prices of commodities.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As some Singhs had already entered one of the forts, Some others sneaked into another fort from the back. As the Singhs occupied many of the Kasur forts, The Muslim Pathans of Kasur came to recognize Singhs' identity. (50)
lines: As some Singhs had already entered one of the forts,
Some others sneaked into another fort from the back.
As the Singhs occupied many of the Kasur forts,
The Muslim Pathans of Kasur came to recognize Singhs' identity.

blocks.text: As soon as the Pathans started barring and locking the fort gates, Than the Singhs started attacking and killing those Pathans. As there spread a great chaos and panic in the whole city, All the Khalsa Dal Singh forces reached the city of Kasur. (51)
lines: As soon as the Pathans started barring and locking the fort gates,
Than the Singhs started attacking and killing those Pathans.
As there spread a great chaos and panic in the whole city,
All the Khalsa Dal Singh forces reached the city of Kasur.

blocks.text: Not only were the Pathans put to sword by the Singhs, Many a Pathan were shot down with the bullets of Singhs' firearms. As the sound of bullet fire kept on getting louder and louder, The Pathans sleeping in basements also woke up from their sleep. (52)
lines: Not only were the Pathans put to sword by the Singhs,
Many a Pathan were shot down with the bullets of Singhs' firearms.
As the sound of bullet fire kept on getting louder and louder,
The Pathans sleeping in basements also woke up from their sleep.

blocks.text: As some had weapons others were without any weapons, Some others woke up from their dozing without picking up weapons. As some carried knives and some other carried daggers, The Singhs shot them down with bullets firing from a distance. (53)
lines: As some had weapons others were without any weapons,
Some others woke up from their dozing without picking up weapons.
As some carried knives and some other carried daggers,
The Singhs shot them down with bullets firing from a distance.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Those Muslim Pathans, as were without any firearms, Soon did they retreat into the safety of their basements. Those who possessed arrows, bows and firearms, They did come out to fight against the Khalsa force. (54)
lines: Those Muslim Pathans, as were without any firearms,
Soon did they retreat into the safety of their basements.
Those who possessed arrows, bows and firearms,
They did come out to fight against the Khalsa force.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs, being ace sharp shooters with their firearms, Many an archer among the Pathans did the Singhs shoot down. The Pathans, being bogged down in taking aims at the Singhs, The Singh sharp-shooters shot them down in an instant. (55)
lines: The Singhs, being ace sharp shooters with their firearms,
Many an archer among the Pathans did the Singhs shoot down.
The Pathans, being bogged down in taking aims at the Singhs,
The Singh sharp-shooters shot them down in an instant.

blocks.text: Those Pathans who rushed out with their swords, With lances and spears did the Singhs strike at them. Killing Pathans at one spot would the Singh move to another, They would soon move to yet another spot after the second. (56)
lines: Those Pathans who rushed out with their swords,
With lances and spears did the Singhs strike at them.
Killing Pathans at one spot would the Singh move to another,
They would soon move to yet another spot after the second.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the Singhs wielding their swords, rushed ahead, Many a Pathan did they slaughter so systematically. As some of the Pathans fled away, others did the Singhs slaughter, Thus did the Divine Guru accomplish the Singhs' mission. (57)
lines: Thereafter, the Singhs wielding their swords, rushed ahead,
Many a Pathan did they slaughter so systematically.
As some of the Pathans fled away, others did the Singhs slaughter,
Thus did the Divine Guru accomplish the Singhs' mission.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After all the Pathans were slaughtered by the Singhs, Then did the Khalsa order looting and plundering of Kasur. Thereafter, rushing into the city from all the directions, The Singhs started committing loot and arson in the city. (58)
lines: After all the Pathans were slaughtered by the Singhs,
Then did the Khalsa order looting and plundering of Kasur.
Thereafter, rushing into the city from all the directions,
The Singhs started committing loot and arson in the city.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Many a street did the Singh chiefs put under siege, Many a palatial Mansion did the Singhs occupy. Many a bigger business concerns did the the Singhs take over, As appeared to be full of expensive merchandise items. (59)
lines: Many a street did the Singh chiefs put under siege,
Many a palatial Mansion did the Singhs occupy.
Many a bigger business concerns did the the Singhs take over,
As appeared to be full of expensive merchandise items.

blocks.text: The Singhs contingent chiefs occupied the main markets, As well as numerous household furnished with luxury items. Sweepers, cobblers and peasants as had followed the Singhs, They, too, helped themselves by looting and plundering. (60)
lines: The Singhs contingent chiefs occupied the main markets,
As well as numerous household furnished with luxury items.
Sweepers, cobblers and peasants as had followed the Singhs,
They, too, helped themselves by looting and plundering.

blocks.text: Gold and silver items alone did the Singhs pick up, Diamonds studded with gems would they reject considering these cheap glass. Brass and alloy utensils no body cared to pick up, Outside the shops would they throw these to be picked up by public. (61)
lines: Gold and silver items alone did the Singhs pick up,
Diamonds studded with gems would they reject considering these cheap glass.
Brass and alloy utensils no body cared to pick up,
Outside the shops would they throw these to be picked up by public.

blocks.text: As the stables were occupied by the Singh chiefs for horses, Bullocks and buffaloes were taken away by the peasantry. Everyone laid their hands on whatever they found worthwhile, Many loaded their horses' backs with reams of cloth. (62)
lines: As the stables were occupied by the Singh chiefs for horses,
Bullocks and buffaloes were taken away by the peasantry.
Everyone laid their hands on whatever they found worthwhile,
Many loaded their horses' backs with reams of cloth.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus did paupers turn as affluent as the kings, Thus did kings turn as impoverished as the paupers. So much did the Khalsa Dal lay their hands upon, That this booty could furnish so many palatial mansions. (63)
lines: Thus did paupers turn as affluent as the kings,
Thus did kings turn as impoverished as the paupers.
So much did the Khalsa Dal lay their hands upon,
That this booty could furnish so many palatial mansions.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

For full three days the Khalsa Dal kept on ransacking Kasur, On the fourth day much of populace too joined the looting spree. The general populace helped themselves to their hearts' content, So much provisions and fabrics had the people taken away. (64)
lines: For full three days the Khalsa Dal kept on ransacking Kasur,
On the fourth day much of populace too joined the looting spree.
The general populace helped themselves to their hearts' content,
So much provisions and fabrics had the people taken away.

blocks.text: Now listen to the tale of the Brahmin (who had brought the Khalsa to Kasur), Who petitioned the Khalsa the next morning after the end of looting. He reminded the Khalsa of having served their own ends, Without bothering about his petition about his wife's abduction. (65)
lines: Now listen to the tale of the Brahmin (who had brought the Khalsa to Kasur),
Who petitioned the Khalsa the next morning after the end of looting.
He reminded the Khalsa of having served their own ends,
Without bothering about his petition about his wife's abduction.

blocks.text: Hari Singh directed him to approach the Khalsa in the afternoon, Asking him to present his case in the Khalsa congregation. Thus did the Brahmin present himself as was he directed, Reminding the Khalsa about his wife's captivity under the Pathans. (66)
lines: Hari Singh directed him to approach the Khalsa in the afternoon,
Asking him to present his case in the Khalsa congregation.
Thus did the Brahmin present himself as was he directed,
Reminding the Khalsa about his wife's captivity under the Pathans.

blocks.text: Asking the Brahmin to lead the Khalsa to the accused's house, The contingent chiefs followed the Brahmin to the targeted location, The moment the Brahmin pointed out the accused Pathan's house, For the second time did the Khalsa slaughter the inmates. (67)
lines: Asking the Brahmin to lead the Khalsa to the accused's house,
The contingent chiefs followed the Brahmin to the targeted location,
The moment the Brahmin pointed out the accused Pathan's house,
For the second time did the Khalsa slaughter the inmates.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Having slaughtered all the wicked Pathan abductors, Brahmin's wife did the Khalsa hand over to the Brahmin. Applauding the Khalsa's noble deed did the Brahmin depart, Delighted, indeed, did he feel having avenged his humiliation. (68)
lines: Having slaughtered all the wicked Pathan abductors,
Brahmin's wife did the Khalsa hand over to the Brahmin.
